diagnosis.cause: The measurement tool's readiness core runs each product startup schema query inside a row_to_json envelope and parses the JSON. PostgreSQL emits oid columns as JSON strings, while the product's schema check compares two of them with numbers (prorettype and tgconstraint), so it refused. The core then threw a code-less error and the harness recorded only SUITE_CASE_FAILED. The product's own runtime path uses the database client directly and is not shown to be affected.
diagnosis.method: Reproduced locally with a stub database client (oid strings fail exactly like J1-R8, numbers pass) and consistent with a read-only reading of the PostgreSQL 16 source (json.c). Not observed on the host; no local PostgreSQL ran.
diagnosis.correction: The J1-R8 run evidence said the product's startup check reports its reason only in the error message; the refusal came from the readiness core wrapping the product check, and the reason was lost there.

changes: after parsing each envelope row, the readiness core restores six allowlisted oid columns (two of them nullable) from strict decimal strings up to 4294967295; any other value refuses with STARTUP_SCHEMA_OID_INVALID
a product refusal keeps the product's own code; the aggregate and io checks after the product assertion refuse with STARTUP_AGGREGATE_UNSUPPORTED and STARTUP_IO_UNSUPPORTED
the harness records a bounded UPPER_SNAKE message, or the first line of an assertion message, when an error carries no code, so a case failure names its reason
rc11.typeSweep: every column of the 13 startup queries was compared between the JSON envelope and the database client's native type; only the six oid columns differ in a way the checks depend on (static reading, not observed on a server)
rc11.unchanged: all 14 adapters (RC10 bytes, including the attestation and the preload shim), the product revision eb532ffd, the RC6 timer rule, every job limit
